Story: I was hauling bags of cement across the site when I spotted the spill—a slick, oily patch right in the middle of the walkway. My supervisor’s voice echoed in my head: “Keep it safe, keep it clean.” I knew if someone slipped, it’d be on me. I reached for the mop, but my phone buzzed. A message from the advocacy group: the city council was about to pass a policy that would cut safety regulations for migrant workers. They needed me to speak up, now, to protect the people who couldn’t risk their jobs by raising their voices. My heart pounded. If I left the spill, someone could get hurt. If I ignored the call, the system would keep grinding down the most vulnerable. Both roles demanded urgency, both demanded my full attention. I stood frozen, mop in one hand, phone in the other, torn between the immediate danger at my feet and the larger injustice looming over us all.
